blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html:
The conditional probability of A given B, written P(A|B), is the probability that A occurs when B is known to have occurred:

P(A|B) = P(A and B) ÷ P(B), defined only when P(B) > 0.

blocks.label: Simplified Explanation
blocks.html: Learning that B happened shrinks the sample space from S to B. P(A|B) is the share of that smaller space in which A also happens. That is why the formula divides by P(B): it rescales the probabilities inside B so that they add to 1 again.

blocks.label: Derivation
blocks.html:
Two results follow in one line each, and both are used throughout §5.5.

General multiplication rule. Multiply both sides of the definition by P(B): P(A and B) = P(B) × P(A|B). By symmetry, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A).

Law of total probability. Let B be any event. The event A splits into two pieces that share no outcomes: “A and B” and “A and not B”. By additivity and then the general multiplication rule:

P(A) = P(A and B) + P(A and not B) = P(A|B)P(B) + P(A|not B)P(not B).

The law says: to get an overall probability, average the conditional probabilities over the groups, weighting each group by its size. It extends to any set of groups B₁, B₂, … , Bₖ that do not overlap and together cover S.

blocks.label: Illustration / Example
blocks.html: In the NCD clinic of §5.2.1, P(diabetes) = 0.2, P(hypertension) = 0.3 and P(both) = 0.1. Among patients known to have diabetes, the probability of hypertension is P(H|D) = 0.1 ÷ 0.2 = 0.5. Among patients known to be hypertensive, P(D|H) = 0.1 ÷ 0.3 = 0.333. The two conditional probabilities differ because they condition on different groups, and neither equals the overall P(H) = 0.3.

points.html: P(A|B) and P(B|A) are different numbers. Confusing them is the root error behind misread screening results (§5.5).
General multiplication rule: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A), valid for any events.
Law of total probability: P(A) = P(A|B)P(B) + P(A|not B)P(not B). It supplies the denominator of Bayes’ theorem (§5.5).
Conditioning is what a diagnostic test does: it moves you from P(disease) to P(disease | result).
